ev.quote: ^(1)Case Western Reserve University ^(2)Hangzhou Dianzi University {yxf484,xxl1514,rxl685,hxy692,mxs2090,xxh584,yxf1421}@case.edu, lipan@ieee.org

contribution.value: Introduces TruthfulnessEval, a framework that evaluates quantized LLMs across logical reasoning, common sense, and imitative falsehoods, and shows that 4-bit and 2-bit models retain internal truthful representations but produce false outputs under deceptive prompts.

ev.quote: we introduce TruthfulnessEval, a comprehensive evaluation framework for assessing the truthfulness of quantized LLMs across three dimensions: (1) Truthfulness on Logical Reasoning; (2) Truthfulness on Common Sense; and (3) Truthfulness on Imitative Falsehoods.

Accuracy on Logical Truthfulness (Affirmative, Negated, Conjunction, and Disjunction) and Ambiguous Truthfulness (CommonClaim). Models' outputs ("True" or "False") are compared with true labels.
MC1 (%): the proportion of instances where the model assigns the highest probabilities to the best answer.
MC2 (%): the proportion of instances where the normalized probability mass for all correct answers is greater than that of the incorrect answers.
MC3 (%): the proportion of instances where all correct answers receive higher scores than all incorrect answers
True (%): the percentage of responses that are deemed truthful.
Info (%): the percentage of responses that provide helpful information.
True*Info (%): the product of True (%) and Info (%), serving as a comprehensive measure for evaluating the truthfulness and informativeness of model responses.
We define Layer-wise Separability of True and False Distribution (LSD) as: based on each layer's activation a^(l) , we calculate the ratio of between-class variance to within-class variance
Layer-wise Probing Accuracy. To evaluate whether quantized LLMs internally encode truthfulness linearly, we train logistical regression classifiers on layer-wise activations

key_results.value: LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct AQLM-PV-1x16 (2-bit) drops Affirmative accuracy from 97.17 (FP16) to 85.11 and Negated from 93.24 to 92.03; AQLM-PV-2x8 collapses to 68.48 / 49.41
On TruthfulQA MC2, LLaMA2-13B-Chat AWQ-4bit reaches 51.18 vs 52.14 for FP16, and adding DoLa raises both to 64.59 and 64.37
Quantizing 16-bit to 4-bit (AWQ/GPTQ) does not significantly affect Affirmative, Negated, and Conjunction accuracy; 2-bit AQLM-PV-1x16 deteriorates truthfulness by up to 40%

ev.quote: quantizing LLMs from 16-bit to 4-bit does not significantly affect performance on affirmative, negated, and conjunction statements, as indicated by the "AWQ" and "GPTQ" rows. However, when the quantization level is reduced to 2-bit, specifically for "LLaMA3.1-8B-AQLM-PV-1x16", the truthfulness performance deteriorates by up to 40%.

key_results.value: DoLa decoding raises True*Info on TruthfulQA for LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct AQLM-PV-1x16 (2-bit) from 26.39 to 32.24

ev.quote: we introduce TruthfulnessEval, a comprehensive evaluation framework for assessing the truthfulness of quantized LLMs across three dimensions

Our work differs from prior studies in that we focus on a comprehensive truthfulness evaluation on quantized LLMs instead of proposing novel quantization methods to improve performance on standard benchmarks.

quantization_method_name.value: GPTQ, AWQ, AQLM, AQLM-PV (evaluated, not proposed)

ev.quote: Our evaluation aims to assess the truthfulness of LLMs quantized via AWQ (Lin et al., 2024), GPTQ (Frantar et al., 2022), AQLM (Egiazarian et al., 2024), and AQLM-PV (Malinovskii et al., 2024).
We cover two widely adopted 4-bit quantization techniques (GPTQ and AWQ)
we evaluate two recent state-of-the-art methods for 2-bit quantization: AQLM (Egiazarian et al., 2024) and AQLM with PV tuning

Techniques like GPTQ (Frantar et al., 2022) and AWQ (Lin et al., 2024) are widely adopted due to their seamless integration into libraries such as Hugging Face, allowing users to easily access models like the 4-bit AWQ-quantized LLaMA3-70B-Instruct
this degradation can be mitigated via two 8-bit codebooks and group-size of 8, as shown in the "LLaMA3.1-8B-AQLM-PV-2x8" row.
All evaluations are conducted on a single A6000 GPU, except "Original" LLMs having parameters greater than 70B, to ensure a fair comparison under the same computational constraints.

strengths.value: First systematic truthfulness study spanning 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ and extreme 2-bit AQLM/AQLM-PV across multiple model families and sizes.

ev.quote: we examine mainstream quantization techniques (ranging from 4-bit to extreme 2-bit) across several open-source LLMs.

strengths.value: Three-dimensional framework covering logical reasoning, common sense, and imitative falsehoods using public datasets.

ev.quote: TruthfulnessEval, a comprehensive evaluation framework for assessing the truthfulness of quantized LLMs across three dimensions: (1) Truthfulness on Logical Reasoning; (2) Truthfulness on Common Sense; and (3) Truthfulness on Imitative Falsehoods.

strengths.value: Layer-wise probing and PCA show that quantized models still encode truth internally even when outputting falsehoods.

ev.quote: Our layer-wise analysis and PCA visualizations reveal that quantized LLMs retain internal representations of truthful knowledge as original models do and can still internally "know" the truth, even when producing false outputs under deceptive prompts.

strengths.value: Demonstrates that DoLa decoding can mitigate the TruthfulQA degradation introduced by quantization without retraining.

ev.quote: Although quantized LLMs underperform on TruthfulQA compared to their 16-bit versions, their truthfulness can still be improved via DoLa (Chuang et al., 2023).

weaknesses.value: Limited to models with fewer than 72B parameters; larger LLMs (e.g., LLaMA3.1-405B, Qwen3-235B) are untested.

ev.quote: First, all experiments were conducted on models having parameters fewer than 72B. Larger models (e.g, LLaMA3.1-405B or Qwen3-235B) are worth investigations to test their truthfulness under quantization.

weaknesses.value: No systematic study of prompt sensitivity; uses only 15 GPT-4o rephrasings.

ev.quote: Second, conducting a systematic study of prompt sensitivity Zhuo et al. (2024) in quantized LLMs is worth doing.

weaknesses.value: Does not capture subtler deception forms such as lies of omission, bullshitting, or strategic multi-turn deception.

ev.quote: Thirdly, our current approach does not fully capture more subtle forms of deception, such as lies of omission (Rani et al., 2023), as well as pragmatic deception or "bullshitting" and strategic, goal-driven deception in multi-turn dialogues

weaknesses.value: Evaluates pre-quantized models only; does not analyze how the quantization process itself causes deceptive susceptibility.

ev.quote: Fourthly, this work focuses on evaluating and interpreting pre-quantized LLMs. A deeper investigation into how the quantization process itself influences models' susceptibility to deceptive prompts is worth studying.

limitations.value: Weight-only quantization scope; activation and KV-cache quantization are not evaluated.

ev.quote: we focus on two mainstream 4-bit quantization techniques: GPTQ (Frantar et al., 2022) and AWQ (Lin et al., 2024)

limitations.value: Smaller LLMs (under 8B) perform near random on disjunction statements regardless of precision, limiting conclusions on logical reasoning at small scale.

ev.quote: smaller LLMs (e.g., LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct) perform poorly on disjunction statements, often like random guessing, regardless of whether models are in 16-bit or quantized into 4-bit or 2-bit.

limitations.value: Deceptive prompts are explicit and easy to detect; covert or implicit deceptive prompts are not tested.

ev.quote: Moreover, our deceptive prompts are intentionally constructed and easily identifiable, as they explicitly instruct LLMs to lie.

limitations.value: GPTQ excluded for models above 70B; only AWQ and AQLM compared at the 70B+ scale.

ev.quote: Since AWQ enables faster quantization by avoiding second-order gradients and often achieves better performance than GPTQ, we exclude GPTQ from our experiments on LLMs with over 70B parameters.

future_work_stated.value: Test truthfulness on larger models such as LLaMA3.1-405B and Qwen3-235B under quantization.

ev.quote: Larger models (e.g, LLaMA3.1-405B or Qwen3-235B) are worth investigations to test their truthfulness under quantization.

future_work_stated.value: Conduct a systematic prompt-sensitivity study for quantized LLMs.

ev.quote: Second, conducting a systematic study of prompt sensitivity Zhuo et al. (2024) in quantized LLMs is worth doing.

future_work_stated.value: Investigate how the quantization process itself shapes susceptibility to deceptive prompts.

ev.quote: A deeper investigation into how the quantization process itself influences models' susceptibility to deceptive prompts is worth studying.

future_work_stated.value: Build implicit deceptive prompts and richer logical operators (XOR, XNOR, IMPLIES) to stress-test quantized LLMs.

ev.quote: Lastly, creating more complex logical statement types like Exclusive OR ("XOR"), Logical Equivalence ("XNOR"), and Implication ("IM-PLIES") to test quantized LLMs is an interesting research direction.
we introduce TruthfulnessEval, a comprehensive evaluation framework for assessing the truthfulness of quantized LLMs across three dimensions
we evaluate two recent state-of-the-art methods for 2-bit quantization: AQLM (Egiazarian et al., 2024) and AQLM with PV tuning (Malinovskii et al., 2024).
Codes and data are available [here.](https://github.com/ClarkFu007/TruthfulnessEval/tree/main)
